_comment: THE TOOL POLICY for brief-agent, the Claude Code run that writes each
day's brief. write.sh passes it with --settings on every run, after jq
strips this comment, so nothing here depends on how Claude Code treats an
unknown key. Edit it here, push, deploy. DECISIONS.md#a-daily-brief-by-email-and-podcast.
WHAT THIS AGENT IS. claude -p, once a day, with web search and web fetch,
rooted in the issues volume, which holds nothing but earlier briefs. It
reads the news and writes one JSON file. Nothing private is in the room:
no vault, no mail, no state, and no credential but its own model-only
token. Prompt injection needs private data, untrusted content and a way
out; this agent has the last two by design and is kept away from the first.
THE HARD BOUNDARY IS THE COMMAND LINE, not this file. write.sh passes
--restricted, which ignores every settings file but this one, refuses
bypassPermissions and confines the file tools to the working directory;
--tools Read,Glob,Grep,Write,Edit,WebSearch,WebFetch, so no Bash, no MCP
and no subagents exist in the session; --strict-mcp-config with an empty
server list, so no .mcp.json can add one; and --permission-mode dontAsk
with --permission-prompts none, so anything not allowed below is refused
rather than asked about. This file narrows what those tools may touch.
WRITES go to ./drafts/ only. The wrapper, not the agent, validates the
draft and moves it into ./published/, which is why ./published/ is
write-denied: an agent that could write there could skip the validator.
Write is governed by the Edit rules, so Edit(./drafts/**) is what lets it
write the draft.
READS of its own token are denied. CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN is in the
process environment, which /proc/self/environ exposes, and the agent has
a way out. The token from `claude setup-token` can only make model
requests, so a leak costs subscription usage, not data, but it is still
denied. ~ is denied too: write.sh gives each run a fresh, empty HOME under
/tmp, but Claude Code may record the claude.ai account's email there.
//state and //audio are tripwires for mounts write.sh also refuses.
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and .claude/ are write-denied at any depth: Claude
Code reads them as standing instructions, and a fetched page that talked
the agent into writing one would be instructing every later run. write.sh
also deletes any it finds before each run.
PATH SYNTAX. './' is the working directory, '//' an absolute path, '~/'
the home directory. A single leading '/' would anchor at this file's own
directory, which is never what is meant here.
CLAUDE.AI CONNECTORS ARE OFF, as on vault-research and for the same
reason: logged into the claude.ai account, Claude Code would otherwise
fetch that account's connectors (Gmail, Drive, the vault) into a session
that reads the open web. write.sh also exports
ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS=false.
